questions.knowledgeNote: Tangent at (x₁,y₁) on x²+y²=a²: xx₁+yy₁ = a²; the normal joins the point to the centre.
questions.question: Q1(a). Find the equations of the tangent and normal to x² + y² = 8 at (2, 2).
questions.solution: Tangent: 2x+2y = 8 → x+y = 4. Normal passes through (0,0) and (2,2): y = x, i.e. x-y = 0. Boxed x+y = 4, x-y = 0 (matches the printed key, book p453).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q1(a); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read); key book p453 = PDF p480

questions.knowledgeNote: At (-6,0) the tangent is vertical and the normal is the x-axis.
questions.question: Q1(b). Find the equations of the tangent and normal to x² + y² = 36 at (-6, 0).
questions.solution: Tangent: -6x+0·y = 36 → x = -6. Normal through the centre (0,0) and (-6,0): y = 0. Boxed x = -6, y = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q1(b); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: For x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 the tangent at (x₁,y₁) is xx₁+yy₁+g(x+x₁)+f(y+y₁)+c = 0.
questions.question: Q1(c). Find the equations of the tangent and normal to x² + y² - 3x + 10y - 15 = 0 at (4, -11).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q1(c); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: A line meets a circle in two coincident points exactly when the perpendicular distance from the centre equals the radius.
questions.question: Q2(a). Show that the line 3x - 4y = 25 and the circle x² + y² = 25 intersect in two coincident points.
questions.solution: Distance of 3x-4y-25 = 0 from the centre (0,0): |−25|/√(9+16) = 25/5 = 5 = radius. A line at distance = radius meets the circle at two coincident points (the tangent), so the intersection is the single point of contact (3,-4). ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q2(a); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same test in general form: distance from the centre must equal r.
questions.question: Q2(b). Prove that the line 5x + 12y + 78 = 0 is tangent to the circle x² + y² = 36.
questions.solution: Centre (0,0), r = 6. Distance = |78|/√(25+144) = 78/13 = 6 = r. Therefore the line touches the circle (tangent) at the foot of the perpendicular (-30/13, -72/13). ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q2(b); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangency is preserved by a common chord line: show the line is at distance r from the second centre, then drop a perpendicular for the contact.
questions.question: Q2(c). Prove that the tangent to the circle x² + y² = 5 at the point (1, -2) also touches the circle x² + y² - 8x + 6y + 20 = 0 and find the point of contact.
questions.solution: Check (1,-2) on the first circle: 1+4 = 5 ✓. Tangent there: x-2y = 5. Second circle: centre (4,-3), r = √(16+9-20) = √5. Distance from (4,-3) to x-2y-5 = 0 is |4+6-5|/√5 = 5/√5 = √5 = r, so the line is tangent to it. Contact = foot of the perpendicular from (4,-3): (4+t, -3-2t) with 4+t+6+4t-5 = 0 → t = -1 → (3,-1). Boxed point of contact (3, -1) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q2(c); book p451 = PDF p478 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y = mx ± a√(1+m²) is tangent to x²+y² = a² for every slope m.
questions.question: Q3(a). Find the tangents to x² + y² = 4 which are parallel to 3x + 4y - 5 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q3(a); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Perpendicular to x+2y = 0 means slope 2.
questions.question: Q3(b). Find the tangents to x² + y² = 5 which are perpendicular to x + 2y = 0.
questions.solution: Slope = 2, a = √5: c = ±√5·√(1+4) = ±5. So y = 2x±5 → 2x-y±5 = 0. Boxed 2x - y ± 5 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q3(b); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Reduce to centre-radius first, then apply |distance from centre| = r with the parallel-line family.
questions.question: Q3(c). Find the tangents to x² + y² - 6x + 4y = 12 which are parallel to 4x + 3y + 5 = 0.
questions.solution: Centre (3,-2), r² = 9+4+12 = 25 → r = 5. Parallel family 4x+3y = k; distance |12-6-k|/5 = 5 → |6-k| = 25 → k = 31 or k = -19. Boxed 4x+3y-31 = 0 and 4x+3y+19 = 0 (both match the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q3(c); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 3x-4y = 1 has slope 3/4, so the perpendicular family has slope -4/3 → 4x+3y = k.
questions.question: Q3(d). Find the tangents to x² + y² - 2x - 4y - 4 = 0 which are perpendicular to 3x - 4y = 1.
questions.solution: Centre (1,2), r² = 1+4+4 = 9 → r = 3. Family 4x+3y = k; distance |4+6-k|/5 = 3 → |10-k| = 15 → k = 25 or k = -5. Boxed 4x+3y-25 = 0 and 4x+3y+5 = 0 (both match the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q3(d); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangency condition for lx+my+n = 0 with x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c = 0: (lg+mf-n)² = (l²+m²)(g²+f²-c).
questions.question: Q4(a). Find k so that the line 4x + 3y + k = 0 may touch the circle x² + y² - 4x + 10y + 4 = 0.
questions.solution: Centre (2,-5), r² = 4+25-4 = 25 → r = 5. Distance = |8-15+k|/5 = 5 → |k-7| = 25 → k = 32 or k = -18. Boxed k = 32 or -18 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q4(a); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The same condition with the parameter buried inside the constant of the line.
questions.question: Q4(b). Find k so that the line 2x - y + 4k = 0 touches the circle x² + y² - 2x - 2y - 3 = 0.
questions.solution: Centre (1,1), r² = 1+1+3 = 5. Distance |2-1+4k|/√5 = √5 → |1+4k| = 5 → 4k = 4 or 4k = -6 → k = 1 or k = -3/2. Boxed k = 1 or -3/2 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q4(b); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangent condition by distance: |r|/√(p²+q²) = a, since the line px+qy = r passes at distance |r| from the origin.
questions.question: Q5(a). Find the condition that the line px + qy = r is tangent to the circle x² + y² = a².
questions.solution: Distance from the centre (0,0) to px+qy-r = 0 is |r|/√(p²+q²). Tangency: |r|/√(p²+q²) = a → r² = a²(p²+q²). Boxed a²(p²+q²) = r² (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q5(a); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Centre (-g,-f), radius √(g²+f²-c): square the distance equation.
questions.question: Q5(b). Deduce the condition that lx + my + n = 0 may be a tangent to the circle x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.
questions.solution: Distance from (-g,-f) to lx+my+n = 0 is |-gl-mf+n|/√(l²+m²); set it equal to √(g²+f²-c) and square: (lg+mf-n)² = (l²+m²)(g²+f²-c). Boxed (lg+mf-n)² = (l²+m²)(g²+f²-c), printed in the key as (g²+f²-c)(l²+m²) = (ln-lg-mf)² — the same statement.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q5(b); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: A normal passes through the centre, i.e. the centre satisfies the line equation.
questions.question: Q5(c). Find the condition that lx + my + n = 0 should be a normal to the circle x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.
questions.solution: The normal must pass through the centre (-g,-f): l(-g)+m(-f)+n = 0 → n = gl+mf. Boxed n = gl + mf (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q5(c); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Slope of the tangent at (x₁,y₁) on x²+y²=a² is -x₁/y₁.
questions.question: Q6(a). Show that the tangents to x² + y² = 100 at (6, 8) and (8, -6) are perpendicular to each other.
questions.solution: At (6,8): 6x+8y = 100 → 3x+4y = 50, slope -3/4. At (8,-6): 8x-6y = 100 → 4x-3y = 50, slope 4/3. Product of slopes = (-3/4)(4/3) = -1, hence perpendicular. ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q6(a); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Both points satisfy the circle; the tangent formula xx₁+yy₁+g(x+x₁)+f(y+y₁)+c = 0 gives the two lines.
questions.question: Q6(b). Prove that the tangents to x² + y² + 4x + 8y + 2 = 0 at (1, -1) and (-5, -7) are parallel.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q6(b); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Circle through the origin with centre (h,k) has no constant term; its tangent at the origin is the line perpendicular to the radius.
questions.question: Q7. Find the equation of the circle whose centre is (h, k) and which passes through the origin, and prove that the tangent at the origin is hx + ky = 0.
questions.solution: r² = h²+k²: (x-h)²+(y-k)² = h²+k² → x²+y²-2hx-2ky = 0. Boxed x²+y²-2hx-2ky = 0. Tangent at (0,0) via xx₁+yy₁-g(x+x₁)-f(y+y₁) with the centre written as (-g,-f) = (h,k): 0+0-hx-ky = 0, i.e. hx+ky = 0 — the line perpendicular to the radius from (0,0) to (h,k), whose slope is k/h. ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q7; book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangency gives l²+m² = 1/a²; the required locus is read straight off that relation.
questions.question: Q8. If the line lx + my = 1 touches the circle x² + y² = a², prove that the point (l, m) lies on a circle whose radius is 1/a.
questions.solution: Distance from (0,0) to lx+my-1 = 0 is 1/√(l²+m²); tangency: 1/√(l²+m²) = a → l²+m² = 1/a². So (l,m) satisfies x²+y² = 1/a², a circle centred at the origin with radius 1/a. ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q8; book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: External contact: distance between centres = r₁+r₂; internal contact: = |r₁-r₂|.
questions.question: Q9(a). Find the conditions for the two circles x² + y² = a² and (x - c)² + y² = b² to touch (i) externally, (ii) internally.
questions.solution: Centres (0,0) and (c,0), radii a and b; distance between centres = |c|. (i) External: |c| = a+b. (ii) Internal: |c| = |a-b|. Boxed a+b = c and a ~ b = c (printed key uses the a ≥ b convention, so |a-b| = c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q9(a); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Write both circles in standard form, then impose the tangency condition; the c⁴ terms cancel and factor.
questions.question: Q9(b). Prove that the two circles x² + y² + 2ax + c² = 0 and x² + y² + 2by + c² = 0 touch if 1/a² + 1/b² = 1/c².
questions.solution: Centres (-a,0) and (0,-b), radii √(a²-c²) and √(b²-c²); distance² between centres = a²+b². Tangency: a²+b² = (r₁±r₂)² = a²-c²+b²-c²+2r₁r₂ → c² = r₁r₂ → c⁴ = (a²-c²)(b²-c²) = a²b²-a²c²-b²c²+c⁴ → a²b² = c²(a²+b²) → divide by a²b²c²: 1/c² = 1/a²+1/b². ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q9(b); book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Tangents from an external point: write y-y₁ = m(x-x₁), impose distance = r, solve the quadratic in m.
questions.question: Q10. Find the equations of the tangents drawn from the point (11, 3) to the circle x² + y² = 65.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q10; book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Chord endpoints from the intersection; the intercept length is the distance between them.
questions.question: Q11. Find the points of intersection of the line x + y - 3 = 0 and the circle x² + y² - 2x - 3 = 0. Also find the length of the intercept made by the line with the circle.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q11; book p452 = PDF p479 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Between two parallel tangents the centre lies on the mid-parallel; the radius is half the separation.
questions.question: Q12. A circle touches the parallel lines 3x - 4y = 7 and 3x - 4y + 43 = 0 and has its centre on 2x - 3y + 13 = 0. Find its equation.
questions.solution: Separation = |7-(-43)|/√(9+16) = 50/5 = 10 → r = 5. Centre lies on the mid-line 3x-4y = (7-43)/2 = -18, i.e. 3x-4y+18 = 0. Solve with 2x-3y+13 = 0: from these, 6x-8y = -36 and 6x-9y = -39 → y = 3, x = -2. Centre (-2,3): x²+y²+4x-6y+(4+9-25) = 0. Boxed x²+y²+4x-6y-12 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q12; book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y = x + c touches x²+y² = a² iff c = ±a√2 — here c = a√2, the '+' branch.
questions.question: Q13. Prove that the straight line y = x + a√2 touches the circle x² + y² = a² and find its point of contact.
questions.solution: Rewrite as x-y+a√2 = 0; distance from (0,0) = a√2/√2 = a = r, so the line is a tangent. Contact = foot of the perpendicular from (0,0): (t,-t) with t+t+a√2 = 0 → t = -a/√2 → (-a/√2, a/√2). Boxed (-a/√2, a/√2) (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q13; book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The power of the origin is +40 > 0, so the origin lies outside the circle and two real tangents pass through it — write y = mx and impose distance = r.
questions.question: Q14. Tangents are drawn from the origin to the circle x² + y² + 10x + 10y + 40 = 0. Find their equations.
questions.solution: Centre (-5,-5), r² = 25+25-40 = 10. Line y = mx → mx-y = 0; distance |-5m+5|/√(1+m²) = √10 → 25(m-1)² = 10(1+m²) → 15m²-50m+15 = 0 → 3m²-10m+3 = 0 → m = 3 or 1/3. Boxed 3x-y = 0 and x-3y = 0 (both match the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q14; book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Length of tangent = √(x₁²+y₁²+2gx₁+2fy₁+c) — the power of the point.
questions.question: Q15(a). Determine the length of the tangent to x² + y² = 25 from (3, 5).
questions.solution: √(9+25-25) = √9 = 3. Boxed 3 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q15(a); book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same power formula with g = 2, f = 3, c = -19.
questions.question: Q15(b). Determine the length of the tangent to x² + y² + 4x + 6y - 19 = 0 from (6, 4).
questions.solution: √(36+16+24+24-19) = √81 = 9. Boxed 9 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q15(b); book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Set the power equal to 5² and solve for k.
questions.question: Q16. Determine the value of k so that the length of the tangent from (5, 4) to the circle x² + y² + 2ky = 0 is 5.
questions.solution: √(25+16+8k) = 5 → 41+8k = 25 → 8k = -16 → k = -2. Boxed k = -2 (matches the printed key); check: r = |k| = 2, centre (0,2), distance to (5,4) = √29, tangent² = 29-4 = 25 ✓.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q16; book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: On the first circle the power of every point is -c, so the tangent to the second circle telescopes.
questions.question: Q17. Show that the length of the tangent drawn from any point on the circle x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 to the circle x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c₁ = 0 is √(c₁ - c).
questions.solution: Let P(x₁,y₁) lie on the first circle: x₁²+y₁²+2gx₁+2fy₁+c = 0, i.e. x₁²+y₁²+2gx₁+2fy₁ = -c. Length of tangent from P to the second circle = √(x₁²+y₁²+2gx₁+2fy₁+c₁) = √(c₁-c). This is independent of P, so all such tangents are equal. ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.15 Ex 15.2 Q17; book p453 = PDF p480 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Chord length 2√(r²-d²) ties the distance d from the centre to the desired slope; here the parameter cancels to a single slope.
questions.question: Q18 (hand-written in this copy). Find the equation of the line through the point (1, -1) which cuts off a chord of length 4√3 m from the circle x² + y² - 6x + 4y - 3 = 0.
questions.solution: Centre (3,-2), r = √(9+4+3) = 4. Chord length 2√(r²-d²) = 4√3 → r²-d² = 12 → d² = 4, d = 2. Line through (1,-1): y+1 = m(x-1) → mx-y-m-1 = 0. Distance from (3,-2): |3m+2-m-1|/√(1+m²) = |2m+1|/√(1+m²) = 2 → (2m+1)² = 4(1+m²) → 4m²+4m+1 = 4+4m² → m = 3/4. Line: 4y+4 = 3x-3 → 3x-4y-7 = 0. Boxed 3x-4y-7 = 0 (matches the answer written beside the question in this copy, book p453). NOTE: this question is hand-written in the margins of this printing (the printed exercise ends at Q17); it is filed for completeness and is not part of the printed numbering. With chord length 2√3 no real line exists (d² = 13 > 20), which fixes the reading 4√3.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, copy of Ch.15 Ex 15.2 (hand-added Q18 after printed Q17); book p453 = PDF p480 (420-dpi zoom read of the hand-written statement and answer)
